summary: Completed the requested broad read-only review. No blocking correctness regression was found in the current orbit output contract, but several validation and data-quality gaps remain. Non-simulator validation passed; live SPEAR render/teleop validation was not run per task constraints.
work_completed: Inspected git status, recent local commits, current diffs, and the requested flashlight/orbit files.
Searched for stale orbit output references, including depth_meters_visualization.mp4 and the old orbit control mappings.
Ran focused validation: python -m unittest tests.test_orbit_collection_validation; 13 tests passed.
Ran focused validation: git diff --check -- requested flashlight/orbit docs, scripts, and tests.
Ran non-simulator help checks for run_orbit_collection.py and run_programmatic_rerun.py.

findings.message: examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:119-146 validates many float CLI options with only inequality checks, so NaN/Inf values are accepted for core options such as --fps, --fov-degrees, --movement-speed, --orbit-duration-seconds, and --idle-period-seconds. A probe confirmed --fps nan, --movement-speed nan, and --orbit-duration-seconds inf are accepted; render mode can then fail later at frame-count math or pass non-finite values into simulator APIs instead of rejecting the CLI input up front.

examples/flashlight/run_programmatic_rerun.py:96-109 has the same CLI validation gap and also omits checks for --movement-speed and --intensity. A probe confirmed --capture-fps nan, --movement-speed -1, --intensity -1, and --outer-cone-angle nan are accepted, which can lead to invalid sleep timing, invalid camera movement/light settings, or simulator API misuse after SPEAR has already launched.

examples/flashlight/run_programmatic_rerun.py:181-188 computes a valid mask for depth visualization but normalizes the full depth array, including non-finite values. A local probe with [1.0, inf, nan] produced white for +inf and emitted a RuntimeWarning on NaN cast, so invalid depth can be visualized as valid far depth instead of being masked consistently like the orbit viridis path does at examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:844-846.

examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:891-898 uses sys.argv in was_arg_supplied even though parse_args/main accept an argv parameter at examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:67 and 1370. The normal CLI path works, but programmatic callers or tests invoking main([...]) in render mode will not get expected spec-overriding behavior for --fps, --orbit-duration-seconds, --width, --height, or --fov-degrees unless those flags are also present in process sys.argv.

examples/flashlight/README.md:162-169 documents percentile clipping and explicit depth visualization bounds but omits --depth-visualization-max-samples, while docs/running_our_example_applications.md:153-155 documents that cap and its default. This leaves the local flashlight README incomplete for large-render tuning.

Orbit render output naming is internally consistent after the recent cleanup: examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:725-729 returns only rgb.mp4 and depth_meters_viridis.mp4, and examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:1338-1349 writes only those videos. Stale depth_meters_visualization.mp4 references were not found in the reviewed product docs/tests/code; remaining depth_meters_visualization references are the separate Rerun stream name.

Generated-output hygiene appears covered for the orbit workflow: .gitignore includes examples/flashlight/orbit_spec.json and examples/flashlight/orbit_collection_output*, and git ls-files shows the current local orbit spec/output artifacts are not tracked.

Live simulator-dependent teleop/render validation was not run, so simulator API behavior, actual frame color/depth content, gamepad input behavior, and end-to-end MP4 generation remain residual risks.

follow_up_recommendations: Add finite/non-negative/positive validation coverage for all numeric CLI options in run_orbit_collection.py and run_programmatic_rerun.py, including tests for NaN/Inf and negative values where invalid.
Mask non-finite depth values in run_programmatic_rerun.py depth visualization before normalization/cast, matching the orbit viridis invalid-pixel behavior.
Replace sys.argv-based override detection in run_orbit_collection.py with parser state or explicit argument-presence tracking that respects parse_args(argv).
Update examples/flashlight/README.md to mention --depth-visualization-max-samples and its default.
Run one live SPEAR orbit render and one live Rerun stream when practical to verify simulator-facing behavior and visual outputs.
